todaysEvents.summary: Trump threatens Oman over Hormuz deal
todaysEvents.delta: AP reported Trump threatened to bomb Oman over its near-term arrangement with Iran to manage Hormuz traffic; the US opposes parts of the joint route-management plan (AP, Aug 18).
AP reported a projectile damaged a ship's engine room as it left Hormuz off Oman, causing a crew casualty; no responsibility was claimed and authorities were investigating (AP, Aug 18).

Iran's parliament speaker said Hormuz will not reopen until Washington lifts the blockade, releases frozen assets, lifts oil sanctions, ends threats and operations, and meets other conditions (AP, Aug 18).

scenarios.label: Base
scenarios.description: Iran and the US could still return to a workable framework normalising Hormuz transit, but AP reported the 60-day deadline passed without a clear settlement and Trump threatened Oman over its near-term route-management arrangement with Iran. Brent moves toward $75-85 only if the arrangement becomes workable, while Qatar's force majeure still limits LNG availability.

scenarios.label: Stress
scenarios.description: No workable full-reopening agreement emerges: AP reported a projectile hit a ship leaving Hormuz with a crew casualty, while Iran still ties reopening to US compliance with the June MoU, blockade relief, sanctions relief and other conditions. Brent holds $78-95 and JKM stays elevated on Qatar force majeure through mid-September.

scenarios.label: Tail
scenarios.description: Trump's threat against Oman over route management, the projectile strike on a ship leaving Hormuz, and Iran's refusal to reopen before US concessions raise the risk of renewed full closure and spillover into the Red Sea/Bab el-Mandeb. Brent returns to $105-135+/bbl and JKM moves above $30/MMBtu as Gulf cargoes become inaccessible.
